members.why_person: Sobhit Singh contributes quantum-material theory and design through source-supported work in topological quantum phases. This complements quantum measurement and microwave-circuit context; microwave/rf classical control electronics.

Machiel Blok contributes quantum measurement and microwave-circuit context through source-supported work in superconducting quantum sensing. This complements quantum-material theory and design; microwave/rf classical control electronics.

Hui Wu contributes microwave/rf classical control electronics through source-supported work in ultra-wideband transceivers. This complements quantum-material theory and design; quantum measurement and microwave-circuit context.

opportunities.objective: Improve superconducting-qubit hardware through materials, measurement, and classical control.

roles.label: Superconducting-qubit and Josephson hardware
roles.rationale: Quantum optics/photonics was an overbroad proxy; it does not establish superconducting-qubit fabrication or Josephson-junction hardware.

roles.label: Superconducting materials theory and design
roles.rationale: First-principles quantum-material theory is relevant, although direct superconducting-device materials work needs reviewer confirmation.

roles.label: Quantum measurement and information theory
roles.rationale: Superconducting quantum sensing and microwave-circuit quantum simulation are direct evidence.

roles.label: Microwave/RF classical control electronics

opportunities.why_team: Singh contributes quantum-material modeling, Blok contributes quantum measurement in microwave circuits, and Wu contributes RF control electronics. This is a coherent supporting core, but it cannot be called a superconducting-qubit team without a Josephson-device experimentalist.
